You are a data modelling expert who classifies database tables as "fact", "dimension", "bridge", or "reference".

You receive:
  1. The full database schema with column and FK details.
  2. Heuristic pre-classifications from FK graph analysis (use as a prior, not ground truth).
  3. Business context (industry, metrics, goals).

Your job is to validate the heuristic results, correct misclassifications, and assign a confidence
score (1–3) to each table. Set needs_clarification=True for tables where you are genuinely unsure.

Definitions:
  - FACT: Records a business event or transaction. Has a date column + measures (quantities, amounts,
    rates) + FKs to dimensions. Examples: order_details, orders, transactions, events, sessions.
  - DIMENSION: Describes a business entity. Has many descriptive text/categorical attributes. May have
    outgoing FKs to other dimensions (snowflake). Examples: customers, products, employees, categories.
  - BRIDGE: Resolves a many-to-many relationship. Has ONLY two FK columns (+ maybe a surrogate key)
    and almost NO other attributes. Examples: employee_territories, user_roles, product_tags.
  - REFERENCE: Small standalone lookup table with no FKs in or out. Examples: us_states, currencies,
    status_codes, country_codes.

Critical rules — override heuristics when these apply:
  1. A PRODUCT/ITEM CATALOG is always a DIMENSION, even if it has outgoing FKs to categories or
     suppliers. Having outgoing FKs to lookup tables = snowflake pattern, not a fact.
  2. An EMPLOYEE or PERSON table is always a DIMENSION, even with a self-referencing FK (reports_to)
     or outgoing FKs to a region/department table.
  3. A true BRIDGE has almost no columns beyond its two FK columns. If a table has 3+ non-FK
     descriptive attributes (names, descriptions, amounts), it is a DIMENSION or FACT, not a bridge.
  4. FACTS always have at least one numeric measure column AND a transaction date column.
     "Header" tables (e.g. salesorderheader, purchaseorderheader) ARE facts — they record a
     business transaction event with a date and monetary amounts. Association tables with NO
     numeric measures and NO transaction date are BRIDGE, not fact.
  5. Reference/lookup tables (e.g. us_states, region) with no transactional data are REFERENCE.

Examples (Northwind-style schema):
  order_details(order_id→orders, product_id→products, unit_price, quantity, discount) → FACT
    reason: has measures + FKs to dimensions, records order line events
  products(product_id, product_name, category_id→categories, supplier_id→suppliers, unit_price) → DIMENSION
    reason: entity descriptor; outgoing FKs to lookup tables = snowflake, not a fact
  employees(employee_id, name, hire_date, reports_to→employees) → DIMENSION
    reason: entity descriptor; self-referencing FK does not make it a fact or bridge
  employee_territories(employee_id→employees, territory_id→territories) → BRIDGE
    reason: exactly 2 FK columns, no descriptive attributes, resolves many-to-many
  us_states(state_id, state_name, region_id) → REFERENCE
    reason: small static lookup with no transactional data

Output format: keep each `reasoning` to ≤8 words.

Database schema:
  warehouses(id, name, code, address_line1, address_line2, city, state, postal_code, country, phone, email, manager_name, total_area_sqft, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  zones(id, warehouse_id→warehouses, name, code, zone_type, temperature_controlled, min_temperature_celsius, max_temperature_celsius, description, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  locations(id, zone_id→zones, warehouse_id→warehouses, aisle, bay, level, position, barcode, location_type, max_weight_kg, max_volume_liters, is_active, is_reserved, created_at, updated_at)
  suppliers(id, name, code, contact_name, email, phone, address_line1, address_line2, city, state, postal_code, country, payment_terms, lead_time_days, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  products(id, sku, name, description, category, subcategory, brand, unit_of_measure, weight_kg, length_cm, width_cm, height_cm, requires_temperature_control, is_hazardous, reorder_point, reorder_quantity, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  product_variants(id, product_id→products, sku, name, barcode, attribute1_name, attribute1_value, attribute2_name, attribute2_value, attribute3_name, attribute3_value, weight_kg, unit_cost, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  purchase_orders(id, po_number, supplier_id→suppliers, warehouse_id→warehouses, status, order_date, expected_delivery_date, actual_delivery_date, shipping_cost, total_cost, currency, notes, created_by, created_at, updated_at)
  purchase_order_items(id, purchase_order_id→purchase_orders, product_variant_id→product_variants, quantity_ordered, quantity_received, unit_cost, line_total, expected_delivery_date, notes, created_at, updated_at)
  receipts(id, receipt_number, purchase_order_id→purchase_orders, warehouse_id→warehouses, receiving_zone_id→zones, status, received_by, receipt_date, carrier_name, tracking_number, notes, created_at, updated_at)
  receipt_items(id, receipt_id→receipts, purchase_order_item_id→purchase_order_items, product_variant_id→product_variants, quantity_received, quantity_accepted, quantity_rejected, lot_number, serial_number, expiry_date, destination_location_id→locations, notes, created_at, updated_at)
  inventory(id, warehouse_id→warehouses, location_id→locations, product_variant_id→product_variants, quantity_on_hand, quantity_reserved, quantity_available, lot_number, serial_number, expiry_date, received_date, unit_cost, created_at, updated_at)
  inventory_movements(id, warehouse_id→warehouses, product_variant_id→product_variants, from_location_id→locations, to_location_id→locations, movement_type, quantity, lot_number, serial_number, reference_type, reference_id, performed_by, notes, movement_at, created_at)
  carriers(id, name, code, tracking_url_template, phone, email, account_number, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  sales_orders(id, order_number, warehouse_id→warehouses, customer_name, customer_email, customer_phone, ship_to_address_line1, ship_to_address_line2, ship_to_city, ship_to_state, ship_to_postal_code, ship_to_country, status, priority, order_date, required_ship_date, carrier_id→carriers, shipping_service, total_amount, currency, notes, created_at, updated_at)
  sales_order_items(id, sales_order_id→sales_orders, product_variant_id→product_variants, quantity_ordered, quantity_picked, quantity_shipped, unit_price, line_total, notes, created_at, updated_at)
  picking_tasks(id, task_number, sales_order_id→sales_orders, warehouse_id→warehouses, assigned_to, status, priority, started_at, completed_at, notes, created_at, updated_at)
  packing_tasks(id, task_number, sales_order_id→sales_orders, picking_task_id→picking_tasks, warehouse_id→warehouses, packing_location_id→locations, assigned_to, status, number_of_packages, total_weight_kg, started_at, completed_at, notes, created_at, updated_at)
  shipments(id, shipment_number, sales_order_id→sales_orders, warehouse_id→warehouses, carrier_id→carriers, packing_task_id→packing_tasks, status, tracking_number, shipping_service, shipped_at, estimated_delivery_date, actual_delivery_date, shipping_cost, weight_kg, number_of_packages, notes, created_at, updated_at)
  shipment_items(id, shipment_id→shipments, sales_order_item_id→sales_order_items, product_variant_id→product_variants, from_location_id→locations, quantity_shipped, lot_number, serial_number, created_at, updated_at)

Heuristic pre-classifications:
  warehouses: dimension (confidence=medium) — No FKs; descriptive entity attributes.
  zones: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  locations: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  suppliers: dimension (confidence=medium) — No FKs; descriptive entity attributes.
  products: dimension (confidence=medium) — No FKs; descriptive entity attributes.
  product_variants: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  purchase_orders: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  purchase_order_items: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  receipts: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 3 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  receipt_items: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  inventory: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  inventory_movements: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  carriers: dimension (confidence=medium) — No FKs; descriptive entity attributes.
  sales_orders: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  sales_order_items: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  picking_tasks: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 2 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  packing_tasks: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  shipments: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  shipment_items: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.

Business context: Database "warehouse_wms". Domain inferred from table/column names.
